transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

What pushed me to come in is I keep jumping at sudden noises. If a door slams, or somebody rolls a suitcase fast through the lobby, it hits me like it’s happening again. My heart starts racing and it takes a minute to calm back down.
Did something traumatic happen to you that these noises remind you of?
Yeah. It was a guest at the counter. Out of nowhere I’ll see this picture of him leaning over and knocking the equipment toward me, even when I’m just answering a normal call.
Since that incident, have you been avoiding things that remind you of it?
Yeah. I’ve been taking the back hallway whenever I can. Going past that spot in the lobby makes my chest tighten up, and I just want to get away from it.
How long has it been since that incident happened?
About two weeks now—since that guest threatened me at the front desk.
Have these reactions been going on for longer than a month?
No, it’s only been about two weeks, since the guest threatened me at the front desk.
When the guest threatened you, did you feel that your life was in danger?
I’m not sure. It all happened so fast—I just knew I was really scared in that moment.
Since this happened, have you had nightmares about it?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed any nightmares, at least not that I can remember.
During the incident, did you think the guest might seriously injure or kill you?
I don’t know if I thought that exactly. I was scared, but it was all so sudden I wasn’t really thinking clearly.
Did the guest threaten to kill you or seriously hurt you?
I can’t say for sure. I remember being frightened, but I don’t clearly remember him saying he was going to kill me or seriously hurt me.
Did the guest physically attack you or make you believe you were about to be seriously injured?
I’m not sure. I remember being scared, but I can’t clearly say whether he actually attacked me or if I thought I was about to be seriously hurt.
Did you believe, in that moment, that you might die?
I’m honestly not sure. I was very scared, but I don’t remember thinking, “I’m going to die,” in that moment.
Were you physically injured during the incident?
I don’t really know. I don’t remember noticing any injury afterward, but I can’t be completely sure.
At the time it happened, did you believe you were about to be seriously injured?
I can’t say for sure. I was frightened, but I don’t clearly remember believing I was about to be seriously injured.
Did you believe the guest was about to seriously hurt you?
I’m not sure. I was scared of him, but I don’t clearly remember thinking he was about to seriously hurt me.
When the guest threatened you, did you believe you were in immediate danger of being seriously hurt?
I’m not really sure. I remember being scared, but I can’t clearly say that I believed I was in immediate danger of being seriously hurt.
Did the guest make a direct threat to seriously harm you?
I don't remember him making a direct threat to seriously harm me. He was intimidating, but I can't recall specific words like that.
During the incident, did you think you might be killed or seriously injured?
I can’t say for sure. I was frightened, but I don’t remember actually thinking I was going to be killed or seriously injured.
Since this happened, has it been hard for you to do your job or handle your usual daily activities?

I’m still going to work, but it’s been harder. My manager shortened a couple of my shifts because I’m slower at the reservation desk, and I keep finding reasons not to go across the lobby when guests need help.
Did the guest ever physically touch you during the incident?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember whether he actually touched me or not.
Did the guest have a weapon during the incident?
I honestly don’t remember seeing a weapon. I was focused on him and trying to get through it, but I can’t say for certain.
